gnosh stop

  Stop a session that runs in the background. The session is a run that gnosh
  --bg, /background or /fork started, named by its ID or the start of one
  (gnosh agents lists them). It is stopped as Esc stops a turn, and given a
  minute to end in good order before it is made to; what it did so far is
  kept: gnosh -r opens it.
  Also typed: gnosh kill.

  Not built yet in this build of gnosh: typing it stops with a message that
  says so.

Usage
  gnosh stop [flags] <session>

Flags
  --cwd <dir>
      Work in this folder instead of the current one.
  -h, --help
      Show help: gnosh's, or after a command's name that command's.
